      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/oct/21/us-vaccine-trial-african-newborns-hepatitis-b</link>

      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026/oct/21/ice-detention-illness-deportation-florida</link>
      <description><p>Flights to third countries where the detainees have no ties are scheduled as early as Wednesday, relatives detail</p><ul><li><p><a href="https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026/oct/15/immigration-trump-midterms-reader-q-a">Send us your questions about immigration and the midterms</a></p></li></ul><p>Relatives of gravely ill detainees at two <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/florida">Florida</a> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/usimmigration">immigration</a> jails say authorities are about to deport their loved ones to unknown countries in Africa despite worsening medical conditions.</p><p>Flights are scheduled as early as Wednesday, according to the families and the immigration advocacy group the Workers Circle, which has been monitoring conditions and speaking with detainees inside two <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/ice-us-immigration-and-customs-enforcement">Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE)</a> facilities in south Florida.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026/oct/21/ice-detention-illness-deportation-florida">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <title>US grants deportation reprieve to migrants from Ukraine and Sudan</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026/oct/19/us-migrants-deportation-ukraine-sudan</link>
      <description><p>DHS says migrants ‘retain protections’ after temporary protected status was set to expire on Monday</p><ul><li><p><a href="https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026/oct/15/immigration-trump-midterms-reader-q-a">Send us your questions about immigration and the midterms</a></p></li></ul><p>More than 100,000 people from Ukraine and Sudan can stay in the United States without immediate risk of deportation, the Department of Homeland Security said, in what amounts to a temporary reprieve after their right to stay in the country was set to expire on Monday.</p><p>Temporary protected status was set to end on Monday for about 101,000 Ukrainians and 1,800 Sudanese. But the DHS said an announcement “will be made at the appropriate time”. Until then, the department said in a written statement, Ukrainians and Sudanese in the US covered by those temporary measures “retain protection”. The department did not indicate how long they could stay or when a final announcement would be made on their status.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026/oct/19/us-migrants-deportation-ukraine-sudan">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/oct/20/flavio-bolsonaro-corrupto-viral-meme-brazil-election-runoff</link>

Plus, 12 valuable lessons about life and death by hospice workers</p><ul><li><p><a href="https://www.theguardian.com/info/2018/sep/17/guardian-us-morning-briefing-sign-up-to-stay-informed"><strong>Don’t already get First Thing in your inbox? Sign up here</strong></a></p></li></ul><p>Good morning. An investigation has revealed that <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/global-development/2026/oct/22/israel-us-made-electroshock-weapons-palestinian-detainees-axon-taser">Israel is using US-made electroshock weapons on Palestinian detainees</a>. The American company Axon is still supplying the Taser weapons despite evidence they have been used to torture prisoners. The news comes as US volunteers including a lawmaker helping Palestinians harvest olives were detained, and <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/oct/21/heidi-levine-palestinians-israeli-settler-attack-west-bank">Heidi Levine revealed more details</a> of her violent assault by Israeli settlers.</p><p>Human rights groups have condemned allegations of the repeated torture and ill-treatment of detainees held in Israeli detention centres and prisons using electric shock devices, with Amnesty calling for restrictions on exports of such devices. A spokesperson for the Israel Defense Forces said the abuse of detainees was strictly prohibited.</p><p><strong>Who was detained by Israel near Nahalin in the occupied West Bank?</strong> The <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/oct/21/israeli-military-detains-brad-lander-rabbis-west-bank-olive-harvest">Israeli military detained</a> about 80 US, Israeli and British volunteers helping Palestinians harvest olives near Bethlehem, including the New York Democratic congressional nominee Brad Lander, several rabbis and Israel’s former deputy attorney general. Soldiers said the area had been declared a closed military zone.</p><p><strong>What more has </strong><strong>Levine said about the Israeli settler attack on her?</strong> The Washington Post photojournalist who was attacked and seriously injured by Israeli settlers on Friday has <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/oct/21/heidi-levine-palestinians-israeli-settler-attack-west-bank">described how she was saved with the help of local Palestinians</a>. Witnesses said thee attack on her ceased only when young men used slingshots to aim stones at the settlers, forcing them back.</p><p><strong>What is the latest development with US diplomats in the Middle E</strong><strong>ast?</strong> The US state department has ordered some diplomats and the families of US government employees <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/oct/22/us-diplomats-told-to-leave-saudi-arabia-amid-houthi-attacks">to leave Saudi Arabia</a>, as it faces a barrage of near-daily attacks from Yemen’s Houthis. Reports have emerged of similar US withdrawals in UAE, Jordan, Qatar and Bahrain amid concerns of a return to conflict with Iran after the midterm elections.</p><p><strong>Where has Elon Musk been spending his election campaign money?</strong> Elon Musk’s Super Pac <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026/oct/21/elon-musk-super-pac-new-york-midterms">has spent more than $500,000</a> in New York’s highly competitive 17th congressional district race to help Mike Lawler, the Republican incumbent, hold his seat. Lawler, a moderate Republican, is fending off a challenge from the Democrat Cait Conley in one of the most-watched races that could determine who controls Congress.</p><p><strong>What has happened with letters containing white powder being sent to Congress? </strong>Nancy Pelosi’s office <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026/oct/21/nancy-pelosi-office-letter-white-powder">received “a suspicious letter”</a> on Wednesday in what appears to be the latest incident of ill-intentioned mailings targeted at US Congress members. The offices of more than three dozen members of Congress across the political spectrum have received envelopes containing white powder in recent days.</p><p><strong>What is Trump’s polling as the election looms? </strong><a href="https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026/oct/21/trump-approval-rating-midterms-poll">Donald Trump’s approval rating has sunk to 36%</a>, the lowest recorded, with most respondents expressing frustration over his handling of the US economy, cost of living and Iran war.       <description><p>Democrats believe circumstances have aligned for them to win a slew of competitive elections in the state</p><p>Mary Peltola’s campaign to represent <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/alaska">Alaska</a> in the <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/us-senate">US Senate</a> has taken her to parts of the massive state’s interior that are inaccessible by road and on the frontlines of the cost-of-living crisis she hopes will make her the first <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/democrats">Democrat</a> to win the seat in nearly two decades.</p><p>She has been to towns where paper towels retail for $40, a half gallon of oat milk goes for $21 and the cost of a new freezer can be quadruple what it is in the state’s largest city, Anchorage, simply because it’s so complicated to get there.       <description><p>Agency declines to reveal in which state latest measles death occurred as it delays reporting other measles deaths </p><p>The US Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) added a third measles death to its dashboard on Wednesday, but the agency would not reveal whether the death occurred in Pennsylvania or another state – which is “notable” as the agency delays reporting other measles deaths, experts say.</p><p>The CDC cited privacy laws in not sharing the name of the state, but experts say there are no privacy concerns in doing so – and this information is important for the public to have as the outbreak continues accelerating, growing by <a href="https://www.cidrap.umn.edu/measles/us-measles-cases-grow-8-1-week-total-4410">8%</a> in one week to 4,410 confirmed cases so far this year, nearly double last year’s count.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026/oct/22/cdc-measles-pennsylvania-state-deaths">Continue reading...</a></description>
